subject: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane
content:
From: Alice Gomez <alice@factoryai.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As we start planning the Private Control Plane (VPC) deployment for FactoryAI, I want to confirm our identity and audit requirements so we can coordinate the integration. High level asks:

- SAML SSO for operator authentication (we run Okta) with assertion attributes for role mapping.
- SCIM provisioning for group -> operator role sync (we have groups: infra-ops, data-platform).
- Short-lived operator credentials for kube/agent actions (15m - 1h TTL preferred).
- Audit events: admin role assumption, token issuance, API key creation, SCIM provisioning changes. We need these events forwarded to our SIEM (Splunk).
- Data retention: audit trail for 2 years, with exportable CSVs and an API for query.

Can you share a recommended mapping pattern (SAML attributes -> Redwood operator roles), and whether Redwood supports cross-account role assumption between our VPC operator role and customer-managed operator service accounts? Also: what artifacts (SAML metadata, SCIM base URL, certs) do you need from us to generate a runbook?

Attached is a sample group list (example-assertion-mapping.csv) for reference.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Gomez
Director of IT, FactoryAI
alice@factoryai.com

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alice Gomez <alice@factoryai.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. This is exactly the level of detail we want early in the runbook. Quick answers and next steps below, then I’ll loop in Ben for the mapping patterns and Laura for audit/retention requirements so we can produce a concise cutover checklist.

High-level: Redwood Private supports SAML-based federated roles + SCIM group sync. We recommend using SAML assertions to assert a stable operator principal (email + role claim) and SCIM to keep group membership in sync. For cross-account role assumption, we support it via a short-lived credential broker in the Private CP that mints time-limited operator tokens tied to the SAML assertion; this can be constrained to specific VPCs and operator actions.

What we need from you to draft a runbook:
- SAML metadata (IdP XML) or metadata URL.
- SCIM base URL and a test service account with temporary credentials.
- Desired mapping table (which groups map to which Redwood operator roles) — your CSV helps.
- Audit forwarding endpoint (Splunk HEC URL) and a sample ingestion key.
- Preferred cutover window (dates/times + blackout windows).

I attached the CSV back (Q: did you mean example-assertion-mapping.csv? I’ve saved a copy). Proposed next step: 30-min alignment call Monday to agree mapping semantics and retention.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: example-assertion-mapping.csv (received)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Alice Gomez <alice@factoryai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane

Hi all — adding a few technical recommendations from the runtime/infra side:

1) SAML assertion design:
- Use a dedicated attribute (e.g., "redwood_role") in addition to standard groups. Pushing a specific role claim simplifies mapping and avoids fragile name-based lookups.
- Include an immutable principal identifier (eduPersonPrincipalName or email) so audits can show who assumed the operator role.

2) SCIM sync pattern:
- Use SCIM for group membership only; do not sync per-user attributes beyond email + externalId. We recommend incremental syncs every 5–15 minutes for near-real-time membership updates.
- Use SCIM PATCH operations for deltas and maintain an operation log on FactoryAI side for reconciliation.

3) Token lifecycle & permissions:
- Issue short-lived operator tokens (default 1 hour, configurable down to 15 minutes).
- Support scope-limited tokens for sensitive actions (e.g., token with scope=read-only vs scope=admin).

4) Audit stream & SIEM integration:
- We can forward events to Splunk HEC; Redwood will emit a stable schema: event_type, actor_email, role_claim, resource, action, timestamp, request_id.
- For large customers we recommend sending both live stream (HEC) and periodic compressed exports as a backup.

I attached a short design note: redwood-privcp-idp-wiring-v1.pdf (internal diagram + recommended assertion mapping).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-privcp-idp-wiring-v1.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, Alice Gomez <alice@factoryai.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane

Thanks Ben — this aligns with what Product & Ops need. A few product constraints and asks to confirm from FactoryAI: 

- Event retention: we store audit events in an append-only store for the retention window you specify (2 years is fine). Export API will support paginated queries and CSV export filtered by time range and event_type. Please confirm whether you need log-level immutability attestation (signed snapshots) or just export/retention guarantees.

- Access controls: Management plane actions (role-grant, token revoke) will be gated behind operator admin role and require MFA on the SAML assertion. If your Okta policies can emit an MFA claim or the assertion includes a flag for MFA, we can enforce that.

- Emergency access / break glass: We support a break-glass workflow that issues an audit-only operator token and requires secondary approval (email + cataloged justification). Want to confirm whether FactoryAI will require this as part of SOC 2 controls.

- Compliance artifacts: I’ve started a collaborative doc with the proposed mapping, event schema, and sample API calls. Link: https://drive.redwoodinc/internal/privcp/idp-wiring-playbook (please add comments).

If this looks good we should schedule the Monday alignment call and I’ll prep the audit export samples and retention SLA language for the contract addendum.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Alice Gomez <alice@factoryai.com>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, infra@acme-corp.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operator identity wiring & audit paths for private control plane

Marissa / Ben / Laura — thanks, this is helpful. A couple quick answers and next steps: 

- We attached our IdP metadata (acme-idp-metadata.xml) and a temporary SCIM test account. Metadata URL: https://saml.factoryai.com/metadata.xml
- MFA: yes, we can include an MFA claim in SAML; we will add a policy that sets a boolean saml:mfa=true for admin flows.
- Retention attestation: we need signed snapshots quarterly for the first year, then annual for the second year. Please indicate how Redwood will provide signed snapshots (digest + signature) in the runbook.
- Cutover window: prefer Sept 7-9 (UTC windows: 00:00-06:00) to minimize impact. We will run a pre-cutover validation in your staging environment two days prior.

Let’s schedule the 30-min alignment call Monday 08/24 at 10:00 PT if that works for your team — that gives us time to exchange metadata and test credentials beforehand.

Thanks,
Alice

Attachment: acme-idp-metadata.xml
